summary: Empirically retested the AI Detect close-button bug on Expo web preview. RESULT: BUG NOT FIXED for the tab-press flow. Tapping the 'AI Detect' bottom tab still navigates to /(tabs)/ai (the empty placeholder) instead of pushing /ai-detect — URL becomes /ai and screen renders as a blank black View. The listeners.tabPress -> e.preventDefault() + router.push('/ai-detect') is NOT stopping the default tab navigation in expo-router/react-navigation on web. Because the AI Issue Detection screen never opens from the tab, the X (back-ai) close-button flow described in the bug cannot execute at all. The two ancillary flows work correctly: (a) Home 'Not sure? Snap a photo' shortcut (testID=ai-detect-shortcut) -> /ai-detect -> back-ai -> Home ✅, (b) Direct navigation to /ai-detect URL ✅. Regression tabs (Requests / Profile / Home) navigate normally. Registration flow works.

issues: Renders as a fully blank black screen if ever reached — no header, no message, no way to escape except tapping another tab. Confusing dead-end state.

action_items: The Tabs.Screen listeners.tabPress fix in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx is not effective on Expo web. Replace the interceptor pattern with a working alternative. Suggested options: (1) Remove the ai tab entirely (set href:null for all users) and rely on the existing Home 'ai-detect-shortcut' banner + a floating action button; (2) Convert the ai tab's screen (/(tabs)/ai.tsx) into the actual AI Detection UI (move the contents of /app/frontend/app/ai-detect.tsx into (tabs)/ai.tsx and change the close button to navigate to /(tabs) instead of router.back); (3) Use a Tabs.Screen with a custom tabBarButton that wraps a Pressable calling router.push('/ai-detect') directly, avoiding the tab framework's default press behavior entirely. Option (2) is the simplest and eliminates the bounce-loop risk because there is no separate stack route to return from.
After chosen fix, retest all 5 scenarios from the review request including the twice-in-a-row loop.
critical_code_review_comments: Expo-router/react-navigation web build does not always honour e.preventDefault() in tabPress listeners; the tab still activates and the target screen mounts. Relying on this pattern is brittle across platforms.
The AiTabPlaceholder returning an empty View with no textual content is a poor fallback — if the interceptor fails (as it does), the user sees a solid black screen with no explanation.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: On Expo web (react-native-web + react-navigation), the tabPress event's preventDefault() does not reliably suppress the underlying tab activation. When the driver taps the AI Detect tab, react-navigation still switches the active tab route to /(tabs)/ai and renders AiTabPlaceholder (an empty View). Although router.push('/ai-detect') is called in the same handler, either it is superseded by the tab-switch navigation or the placeholder mounts on top of the freshly pushed stack. The observable result matches the original bug report: the user cannot reach the close button via the tab. Reproduction: 1) Register/login as driver, 2) On Home, tap the 'AI Detect' item in the bottom tab bar, 3) Observe URL changes to /ai and screen goes fully black with no AI Detection header and no back-ai testID. Mitigation: Do not rely on tabPress preventDefault on web. Either eliminate the separate /ai-detect route by placing the AI screen directly in (tabs)/ai.tsx (recommended — simplest, no navigation trickery), or replace the AI tab with a custom tabBarButton whose Pressable calls router.push('/ai-detect') without going through react-navigation's tab dispatcher.
